newsitem.title: USA: Rubin - U.S. economy on "very good path".
newsitem.headline: Rubin - U.S. economy on "very good path".

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin on Thursday said the U.S. economy was on a healthy track, and said inflation was unlikely to pick up.
"We're really on a very good path," Rubin said in response to a question at a meeting of the President's Export Council.
He said workers' wages have started to head higher after years of stagnation, but added, "I don't see signs of a re-ignition of inflation."
Rubin added that based on discussions with people in the private sector there does not seem to be an anticipation of inflation there either.

Asked by reporters about the likelihood of sales of International Monetary Fund gold to deal with the debt of poorer countries, the Treasury secretary responded that the administration expectation is unchanged.
He said that in the final analysis, he believes that the gold sales are needed and are the "mechanism that is going to happen."
